lesson.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes
lesson.goal: build a REST API with FastAPI: GET and POST endpoints with Pydantic models, run with uvicorn

sources.title: Python FastAPI Tutorial: Build a REST API in 15 Minutes

steps.title: Install FastAPI and run hello world
steps.instructions: Run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`, create main.py with `app = FastAPI()` and an `@app.get("/")` route returning a small JSON dict. Start it with `uvicorn main:app --reload` and open the URL in the browser.

targets.caption: Create the FastAPI app instance
Decorator defining the GET route for the root path
Server is up; open this URL

explanations.topic: Uvicorn is the server that runs FastAPI apps
Path decorator for the HTTP GET method
The root path "/" calls the function
uvicorn main:app means file name, then app object
--reload restarts the server when the file changes

hints: Install both packages first: pip install fastapi uvicorn.
In main.py, import FastAPI, then create it with app = FastAPI().
Decorate a function with @app.get("/") and return a dict like {"Hello": "World"}.
Run uvicorn main:app --reload from the folder that contains main.py, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000.
common_mistakes: Installing fastapi but not uvicorn, which gives 'uvicorn: command not found'.
Running uvicorn from a different directory than main.py, which gives 'Could not import module "main"'.
Mismatching the module:app names, e.g. uvicorn main:App when the variable is app ('Attribute "App" not found').
Writing app = FastAPI without the parentheses, so the class is never instantiated.
Forgetting the @ on the decorator, or using @app.get without the "/" path.

steps.title: Add POST endpoint to create items
steps.instructions: Add an `items = []` list and an `@app.post("/items")` handler taking `item: str` that appends it and returns the list. Test with `curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'`.

targets.caption: Empty in-memory list holding the items
POST endpoint on the /items path
Send a POST with ?item=apple from a second terminal

explanations.topic: What routes are in FastAPI
POST request to the /items path
Simple-typed function args become query parameters
Returning the whole list to see results
Passing the item as a URL query parameter with curl

hints: Create a module-level `items = []` list above your new route so it persists between requests.
Decorate a function with `@app.post("/items")` and give it a parameter `item: str`; FastAPI treats it as a query parameter.
Inside the function call `items.append(item)` and `return items`.
Keep uvicorn running (with --reload) and run in a NEW terminal: curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple' and you should see ["apple"].
common_mistakes: Using @app.get instead of @app.post, so curl -X POST returns {"detail":"Method Not Allowed"}.
Defining `items = []` inside the function, so the list resets on every request.
Forgetting the ?item=... query string, giving a 422 'field required' error.
Not quoting the URL in the shell, so `?` or `&` gets interpreted by the shell.
Running curl in the same terminal as uvicorn, or forgetting to restart uvicorn without --reload.

steps.title: Add GET item by ID endpoint
steps.instructions: Add `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` with an `item_id: int` parameter returning `items[item_id]`. Re-add items, then `curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/0`.

targets.caption: New GET endpoint with an item_id path parameter
Type hint makes FastAPI convert the path value to int
Fetch the first item by index

explanations.topic: Path parameters in curly braces map URL segments to function arguments
Server reload resets the in-memory items list
Type hints let FastAPI convert path parameters automatically
Requesting a non-existent index causes an internal server error

hints: Use the same @app.get decorator, but put the variable part of the path in curly braces.
The name in the braces must match the function parameter name, e.g. /items/{item_id} and get_item(item_id: int).
Add the int type hint so '0' from the URL becomes the integer 0 for indexing.
Saving the file reloads the server and empties the list, so POST a couple of items again before calling curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/0.
common_mistakes: Testing right after saving without re-adding items: the list was reset, so index 0 gives an Internal Server Error (IndexError).
Path placeholder name differs from the function parameter (e.g. {id} vs item_id), so FastAPI treats it as a query param and returns 422.
Omitting the int type hint, so the index is a string and items[item_id] raises TypeError.
Using parentheses or no braces in the path, like "/items/item_id", which matches only that literal URL.
steps.run_command:
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=apple'
curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?item=orange'
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/items/0

steps.title: Raise 404 with HTTPException
steps.instructions: Import `HTTPException` from fastapi and raise `HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=...)` in the get-by-id handler when the index is out of range. Curl a missing id (e.g. /items/47) to see the 404 detail.

targets.caption: Import HTTPException from fastapi at the top of the file
Raise a 404 when the item index doesn't exist
The curl response shows the 404 detail

explanations.topic: Why an internal server error isn't helpful for a missing item
HTTP status codes: missing item is a client error
404 Not Found is the right response code
The detail parameter explains why the item wasn't found

hints: Before returning the item, check whether item_id is a valid index into your items list.
Add HTTPException to your existing `from fastapi import ...` line.
In the else branch: `raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Item {item_id} not found")`.
Re-run the curl request for an ID larger than your list. You should get JSON with a "detail" key, not a traceback.
common_mistakes: Using `return HTTPException(...)` instead of `raise`. This returns a 200 response instead of a 404.
Forgetting to import HTTPException, which causes a NameError when the missing item is requested.
Writing the condition as `item_id <= len(items)`. That is off by one and still crashes at index len(items).
Leaving out the `f` prefix so the detail shows literally `{item_id}`.
Not restarting uvicorn (or not running it with --reload), so the old code still returns 500.

steps.title: List items with limit query parameter
steps.instructions: Add `@app.get("/items")` with a `limit: int = 10` query parameter returning `items[0:limit]`. Test with `curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3'`.

targets.caption: List endpoint with a limit query parameter
Request the first 3 items

explanations.topic: Path vs query parameters; item in create_items is a query string
FastAPI converts query string values to the annotated type (int)
Same /items URL, different HTTP method routes to a different function
Default value for an omitted query param comes from the function signature

hints: Add a new GET route on the same "/items" path you used for POST.
Give the function a parameter `limit: int = 10`. FastAPI treats it as a query parameter.
Return `items[0:limit]`, then POST a few items and run `curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/items?limit=3'`.
common_mistakes: Reusing the function name create_items, which overwrites the earlier endpoint.
Using @app.post instead of @app.get, so the curl GET returns 405 Method Not Allowed.
Forgetting the type hint, so limit stays a string and slicing raises a TypeError.
Not quoting the URL in the shell, so `?` is mangled by globbing.
Restarting the server and forgetting that the in-memory list is now empty, so you get [].

steps.title: Use Pydantic Item model for requests
steps.instructions: Import `BaseModel` from pydantic, define `class Item(BaseModel)` with `text: str` and `is_done: bool = False`, and use Item as the POST body type and get-by-id return type. POST JSON with `curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"apple"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/items`.

targets.caption: Define the Pydantic Item model
Accept an Item in the POST body
Response is now a JSON object

explanations.topic: Why Pydantic models: structure, validation, docs, IDE completion
Model arguments are read from the JSON body, not query params
Default value is_done=False filled in automatically
Removing a default makes a field required and validated

hints: Import BaseModel from pydantic and subclass it to create Item.
Give Item two fields: text: str and is_done: bool = False.
Change create_item's parameter type from str to Item, and annotate get_item's return as -> Item.
Call the endpoint with a JSON body: curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"text":"apple"}' http://127.0.0.1:8000/items (drop the ?item= query parameter).
common_mistakes: Still sending the item as a query parameter (?item=apple), which now returns a 422 error.
Forgetting the Content-Type: application/json header in curl.
Using single quotes inside the JSON payload, which makes the body invalid JSON.
Defining Item as a plain class without inheriting from BaseModel.
Leaving get_item's return annotation as str, so the response no longer matches the stored Item objects.

steps.title: Add response models to routes
steps.instructions: Add `response_model=Item` to the get-by-id decorator and `response_model=list[Item]` to the list decorator. Let uvicorn reload and confirm it still runs.

targets.caption: Declare the response model on the decorators

explanations.topic: Modeling responses with the same Pydantic BaseModel used for requests
response_model is an argument to the route decorator
Using list[Item] as the response model for a list endpoint
Response models tell clients the endpoint's response shape

hints: The response model goes in the @app.get(...) decorator, not in the function signature.
Add a keyword argument named response_model to the decorator, after the path string.
Use response_model=Item for the get-item route and response_model=list[Item] for the list route.
If list[Item] errors, you are on Python < 3.9: use List[Item] from typing instead.
common_mistakes: Writing response_model as a function parameter instead of a decorator argument.
Using response_model=Item on the list endpoint, which fails validation because a list is returned.
Spelling it responseModel or response-model instead of response_model.
Using list[Item] on Python 3.8 or older, causing a TypeError at startup.
Returning dicts missing required Item fields, which now raises a response validation error.

steps.title: Explore interactive docs
steps.instructions: Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs, use Try it out on POST /items and Execute it. Also visit /redoc and /openapi.json.

targets.caption: Click Try it out on POST /items, edit the body, then Execute
The real response from your API appears here
Link to the raw OpenAPI JSON schema

explanations.topic: FastAPI auto-generates interactive docs for free
Swagger UI at /docs lists endpoints, methods, parameters
Execute shows the curl command and sends a real request
/redoc is an alternative docs view
openapi.json describes all paths, schemas and responses for client generation

hints: Make sure your uvicorn server is still running, then open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in the browser.
Expand the POST /items endpoint, click 'Try it out', edit the JSON request body, and press 'Execute'.
Scroll down to see 'Response body'. Then try http://127.0.0.1:8000/redoc and http://127.0.0.1:8000/openapi.json.
If the page won't load, check the terminal for the 'Uvicorn running on' line and the port number.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to click 'Try it out' first, so the request body stays read-only.
Sending a request body that doesn't match the Pydantic Item model, which returns a 422 validation error.
Stopping the uvicorn server or opening the wrong port, so /docs fails to load.
Typing '/doc' or '/docs/' with a typo instead of '/docs'.
Expecting created items to persist after a server restart (they live in an in-memory list).
